# Translate or modernize

Read the short editorial policy and this work's and target edition's notes.
Imagine the original author born as a contemporary speaker of the target
language and becoming a novelist: how might they have written this work?

Preserve the story and larger narrative structure. Do not abridge, add scenes,
or reorganize the work. Sentence boundaries and paragraphing are not fixed.
Translate visible labels too; do not invent headings for unlabeled nodes.
Work-specific choices and experiments belong in notes, not new global rules.

Save the work as files, record the model label actually available and capture
this prompt, any session instructions, relevant notes and output hashes with
record-run. Report unfinished or unverified work honestly. A draft is not an
approved publication. No paid API calls unless explicitly authorized.
Translate the synthetic Last Ferry fixture into Japanese for annotation tests, including its labels and the branch introduction. This is an unreviewed development sample, not a published classic.

inputs.text:
# Editorial policy

## Aim

Translate or modernize as though the original author had been born a contemporary
speaker of the target language and become a novelist. This is a working editorial
question, not a claim that we can reconstruct a uniquely correct answer.

## Scope

Choose public-domain works that the maintainer expects contemporary readers to
enjoy once the linguistic distance is reduced. Selection is a matter of taste and
project scope, not a universal judgment about a book's merit or accessibility.
Do not select a work that would require turning it into a substantially different
book to achieve that aim.

Preserve the story, characters, setting, narrative viewpoint, events and larger
narrative organization. Abridgement, new scenes, reordered chapters and structural
adaptation are outside the present scope. Retain the source's meaningful
Book/Volume/Chapter divisions and their order; translate existing book titles and
headings without inventing missing ones. Publishing the whole work as a single
EPUB does not erase its internal divisions. Contemporary language does not mean
moving the story into the present day.

Sentence boundaries, paragraphing and phrasing may change freely in service of
that aim. Do not preserve an awkward sentence merely to retain correspondence.
Do not mistake completeness for sentence-by-sentence literalism.

No universal house style, target sentence length, mandatory model or prescribed
translation procedure is established here. Record work-specific decisions only
when experience shows that they are useful. A whole new translation is a normal
possible revision, not a failure of the workflow.

# The Last Ferry — work notes

This is a synthetic software fixture carried forward from the starter, not a
classic. Its main purpose is to test nested and unlabeled nodes, Unicode,
prose on branches, translation fields, snapshot anchoring and margin notes.
The crossing intentionally has a different paragraph structure in Japanese.
Do not include the fixture in the finished-books catalogue.

## Observations
The existing English demo changes the ferryman's name in chapter two. Keep
that test case available; it is not a proposed editorial convention.

# Japanese fixture

This is a new synthetic-fixture translation for UI testing. Names use マーラ
and レノ consistently. No human review has taken place. Paragraph lengths need
not match the English fixture. These are not project-wide choices.
